summary: The portal comparison surface now consumes the live ready-engine registry, displays per-engine answers with model/source telemetry, and keeps Contract v2 approval, execution output, tools and audit diagnostics visible in the chat workflow. Mutation responses without a Contract v2 binding fail closed instead of showing an apply button that cannot be safely executed.

files.purpose: Render only ready engines, model selection, benchmark cards, token/latency/tool/audit metrics, persistent execution output, and Contract v2 failure diagnostics.
Return normalized engine/model/telemetry/context and the Contract v2 approval binding consumed by the portal.
Cover live runtime connection, exclusion of configured/unavailable engines, approval/apply/run, prose recovery, persistent output and comparison metrics.

checks.summary: All six live browser tests passed, including explicit exclusion of configured/unavailable engines, comparison metrics/audit UI and approval execution visibility.

risks: The browser comparison is limited to engines whose live readiness endpoint reports ready; unconfigured providers are intentionally omitted and are not represented as fake working engines.
followUps: P2-T2 remains the next execution-safety milestone: isolate each mutating task in its own Git worktree before concurrent multi-agent execution.
